previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for progressive shortness of breath over one week, culminating in dyspnea at rest. Initial concern for pulmonary embolism or infection led to a CT angiogram, which ruled out PE but revealed ground-glass opacities suggestive of healthcare-associated pneumonia. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and showed clinical improvement. Pulmonary function tests confirmed worsening restrictive and obstructive lung disease due to progression of bronchiolitis obliterans associated with GVHD. Prednisone was increased from 25 mg to 40 mg daily and then tapered, and ruxolitinib was initiated as part of GVHD management. He completed a 10-day antibiotic course, remained stable, and was discharged home on his baseline immunosuppressants, ruxolitinib, and a prednisone taper. Follow-up was arranged for repeat imaging and ongoing oncology and pulmonary care.
